card.name: Inside spasm words like bronchospasm
card.fires_on: The piece just before the ending -spasm/-asm in words such as bronchospasm, vasospasm, coronary artery spasm and sphincter of Oddi spasm. It also fires on 'to' before 'contract' in uterine cramp text.

modes.label: Split spasm words
modes.description: A piece of a spasm word (sp, ch, osp) right before the remaining -asm or -ospasm ending.
modes.example: may produce severe bron<<ch>>ospasm in asthmatic patients.

modes.label: Muscle contraction wording
modes.description: The word 'to' right before 'contract' when describing muscles tightening.
modes.example: a chemical that causes the muscles of the uterus<< to>> contract.

card.writes: It pushes toward 'smooth' and 'contracted' (muscle contraction terms) and away from NSAID-like starts such as 'aspir', 'ib' and 'NS'.
card.plain: It lights up when a word for a muscle spasm, like bronchospasm, is still being spelled out.
